newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Playboy son of Romania's Ceausescu dies.
newsitem.headline: Playboy son of Romania's Ceausescu dies.

text.p: Nicu Ceausescu, the hard-drinking playboy son of Romania's late communist dictator Nicolae Ceausescu, died in hospital in Vienna on Thursday, a hospital spokeswoman said.

Nicu, 45, the youngest of the three children of Nicolae and Elena Ceausescu, was known as a womaniser who squandered vast sums of public money at the gambling tables of Las Vegas and other casino towns.
"Mr Ceausescu died at 6 a.m. (local time, 0400 GMT) this morning," the spokeswoman at Vienna's General Hospital told Reuters. She gave no further details but said a statement was in preparation.

Nicu, who was suffering from liver disease, was admitted to Bucharest university hospital on September 14 with internal bleeding and was flown to the Austrian capital last week for specialist treatment.
He was believed to be on a waiting list for a liver transplant.

Nicu was being groomed as his father's successor before a violent revolution toppled the Stalinist dictatorship in December 1989. Nicolae Ceausescu and his wife, Elena, were shot by firing squad on Christmas Day, ending their ruthless 24-year rule.
Nicu, a physicist, was the communist party boss in the central Romanian county of Sibiu when the revolution erupted.
He was sentenced to 20 years in jail on charges of mass murder after ordering the repression of protests in Sibiu.
His brother, Valentin, had lobbied hard to win Nicu's release from jail. Romanian authorities freed Nicu on health grounds in November 1992.
Nicu is also survived by his sister, Zoe.
